To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the cDNA sequence of the human placental CRF gene was isolated and characterized, (2) the cDNA was used to transcribe sense-strand hCRRNA which was translated and processed in vitro, (3) sequence analysis of the cRNA confirmed the exon-intron boundaries predicted from the genomic structure, and (4) the translated preprohCRF gene product contained a functional signal sequence that suggested that placental CRF peptide is secretory in nature.

the cDNA sequence of human placental CRF is identical to that of hypothalamic CRF, that the placenta expresses two different forms of CRF mRNA, and that the preproCRF peptide contains a functional signal sequence.
the cDNA encoding preproCRH has been cloned from human placental mRNA and that in vitro processing of this prepropeptide results in the formation of a mature CRH peptide.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular biology of corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH) in the human placenta.
the molecular characterization and processing of human CRH and the elucidation of its biological role in pregnancy.
the structure, regulation, and function of human corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the human placental CRF is a 41 amino acid peptide, which is processed from a 170 amino acid precursor protein.
preprocorticotropine releasing hormone (CRH), the precursor of CRH, contains a signal sequence that is cleaved to produce the 41 amino acid peptide CRH.
the preproCRF gene product contains a functional signal peptide, which suggests that the placental CRF peptide is capable of secretion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the placental CRH is processed in the endoplasmic reticulum by the signal peptidase and the signal peptide is removed.
we have cloned and sequenced a cDNA encoding human preproCRH and demonstrated its processing in vitro.

the placental CRH is a peptide of 41 amino acids with the sequence: Ser-Asp-Glu-Arg-Val-Asp-Gly-Glu-Leu-Asp-Val-Glu-Asp-Gln-Val-Asn-Leu-Arg-Asn-Val-Glu-Leu-Gln-Glu-Glu-Val-Gly-Arg-Val-Leu-Leu-Leu-Gly-Gln-Gly-Glu-Arg-Gly-Lys
The main takeaway from our work is that
placental CRF is a prohormone, not a pro-prohormone as previously thought.
the preproCRF gene product contains a functional signal sequence and thus is secreted.
preprohCRH mRNA can be translated in vitro and that it is processed into the mature peptide, hCRH.
